rule: Top-level / file-level code (outside any function or type): the caller is the file's module ID. Languages with a module qualifier use it (Python module, JS/TS module, Lua module, OCaml/Haskell module, Rust module path `crate::a::b`, Groovy `pkg.Script#run`). Languages without one (Ruby, PHP, C, C++, ObjC, Zig file scope) use the file path below the scan root without extension (`lib/devise/rails/routes`). An empty caller or `<global>` is a wrong caller.
notes: PHP has no module qualifier → file-level caller is the path below src/ without extension: public/index. $kernel = new Kernel(...) types the receiver (decision A, `= new T(...)`) → App.Kernel#boot high. boot_env is a global-namespace free function → bare ID, high. The relative name App\Kernel in a non-namespaced file is \App\Kernel. getenv is a builtin in the global namespace: a bare name not found in the scan → low (tier text; PHP has no builtin rule like Python's builtins.len). call_type: SPEC lists direct|method without defining them; this corpus uses method for every callee of the form Type#m / recv.m / .m (instance and static member calls) and direct for free functions, bare names and named nested functions.
